prompt.en: Can you think of a resource in your region that is scarce but used wastefully? Identify the resource, describe how it is wasted, and suggest how it could be managed better. (3 marks)

label.en: Identifies a specific locally relevant scarce resource — water, electricity, fuel, fertile soil, groundwater and similar

level1.en: What is one thing your region never seems to have enough of — in summer, or during exams?

clue.en: Think of what gets rationed, cut or argued over locally: drinking water, power cuts, petrol prices, vanishing farmland.

level2Template.en: A scarce resource in my region is ___, which remains in short supply during the summer months.

label.en: Describes concrete wasteful use — running taps, idle pumps, lights left on, stubble burning, leaky pipes and similar evidence

level1.en: Where have you actually seen this resource slip away unused — at home, on the street, on a farm?

clue.en: Look for the small leaks: taps left running, shop shutters open with AC blasting, crop residue burnt instead of returned to the soil.

level2Template.en: It is wasted when people leave ___ running, when leaks go unrepaired, and when fields receive more water than the crop actually requires.

label.en: Suggests realistic management steps such as pricing/rationing, repair and maintenance, recycling or reuse, efficient technology, or awareness campaigns

level1.en: What single rule, repair or habit would save the most of it first?

clue.en: Better management can mean fixing leaks, metering and fair pricing, harvesting rainwater, reusing waste, or simply teaching users why every drop counts.

level2Template.en: It can be managed better by ___, together with public education in its economical use.

text.en: A resource can be scarce and still be wasted. Water is a common example in many regions.
A scarce resource in my region is ___, which remains in short supply during the summer months.
It is wasted when people leave ___ running, when leaks go unrepaired, and when fields receive more water than the crop actually requires.
It can be managed better by ___, together with public education in its economical use.
